name: R. G. LeTourneau

summary.text: Robert Gilmour LeTourneau, an earthmoving-equipment manufacturer, is described by LeTourneau University and Christian writers as having lived on 10 percent of his income and given 90 percent away to Christian causes through the LeTourneau Foundation, which supported Bible schools and camps and the technical institute that became LeTourneau University.

facts.claim: LeTourneau University's library exhibit and other Christian sources describe LeTourneau as living on 10 percent of his income and giving 90 percent away; his foundation supported Bible schools, Bible camps and an international conference center.
facts.quote: living on 10% of his income and giving 90% of it away

facts.claim: LeTourneau founded the LeTourneau Technical Institute, which later became LeTourneau University.
facts.quote: Later, his technical institute became LeTourneau University.

openQuestions: A 1959 figure that the foundation still held roughly $40 million after donating $10 million appears in a secondary essay; the foundation's own filings were not found. No source links LeTourneau's giving to the named political-religious groups (Spiritual Mobilization, Christian Freedom Foundation), so no connection is recorded.
